summary: Players will like naming stores they actually shop at (Walmart, Amazon, Costco, Home Depot, CVS, Walgreens come fast), and Target missing at #11 is a real surprise. What they won't love: Schwarz Group and JD.com are unknown names, and every other famous store they try (Lowe's, Best Buy, IKEA, Tesco) costs a life, so most games end at zero lives with 6 or 7 found.
reasons: Casual replays: a US player found 7 and lost lives on Target #11, Lowe's #14, Best Buy, Macy's and IKEA, each showing its revenue; a UK player found 6 (Lidl and Boots score, Tesco, Asda and Sainsbury's cost lives); a mixed run found 9. A fan found all 10 with 2 lives lost.
Data matches Deloitte's FY2023 retail revenue and the prompt names the measure, so Amazon at #2 (retail sales only) is fair. All 10 have facts, and the Schwarz fact names Lidl.
Fairness is only 3: the 100-deep pool makes nearly every famous store a costed miss. That suits Blitz, where a casual run scored 25 of 33 names.
fixes: "tj maxx", "tjmaxx", "t.j. maxx" and "tk maxx" get "That doesn't look like an answer." (the junk detector): add TJ Maxx, T.J. Maxx, TK Maxx, Marshalls and HomeGoods as aliases of TJX Companies (#24), as Zara is on Inditex.
"kmart" offers Walmart as a misspelling (only before Walmart is found); Kmart is another chain and should be free.

Builder's flag confirmed: "store"/"stores" offer Ross Stores, "supermarket(s)" Wm Morrison Supermarkets, "wholesale" BJ's Wholesale Club, "mart" E-mart, all as a did-you-mean (a life only if confirmed). Treat these as category words.
"morrisons" only reaches Wm Morrison Supermarkets through did-you-mean, and "m&s" is not recognized: add Morrisons and M&S as aliases.
Figures are Deloitte FY2023; refresh when the Wikipedia page moves to the FY2024 Global Powers of Retailing.
